plot: The rain hammered against the slate roof of the cottage, a relentless drumming that mirrored the ache in my bones. It wasn’t the weather that bothered me, though. It was the silence. A silence thicker than the stew I was attempting to coax from a rabbit, a silence born of absence. The King’s men hadn’t been back in three days. Three days since they’d dragged Gareth – Gareth, bless his foolish heart – off to the dungeons. He’d been arguing with a tax collector, a pointless squabble over a handful of silver, and now he was facing a sentence of a hundred years, or worse. I stirred the pot, adding a pinch of dried rosemary, its scent doing little to dispel the gloom. The vegetables were coming along nicely, a medley of root vegetables and wild mushrooms I’d gathered myself. I hated this cottage. Hated the damp, hated the solitude, hated the way the shadows seemed to lengthen and twist with every passing hour. It was a cage, built of grief and duty. I plated the rabbit, drizzling it with honey and sprinkling it with herbs. It looked… almost beautiful. Almost. Almost as beautiful as a distraction. A way to keep my hands busy, my mind occupied. To pretend, for a little while, that things weren't as bleak as they were. I took a bite, chewing slowly, savoring the flavor. It was good. Too good. Too good to be forgotten.
